newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Thursday with instituions borrowing heavily to prepare for a domestic A share issue on Friday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 12.03 percent from 9.9 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market surged to 10.7 million lots from 3.28 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Daye Special Steel Co, a domestic A share company, will issue shares on the Shenzhen stock exchange on Friday.
"Institutions bought heavily on the repo market today because of the issue," said one trader.
"But rates are unlikely to rise again on Friday due to the technical correction on Shanghai's A share market," he added.
Shanghai's A share index lost 9.237 points or 0.78 percent to 1,168.466 points on Friday after recent heavy gains.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Thursday on a lack of fresh market-moving news, traders said. The market has been on a correction since Monday.
The most active 10-year bond maturing in June 2006 fell to 117.20 yuan from 117.86 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 713,531 lots from 0.96 million.
"With a vacuum of market-moving news, the technical correction starting on Monday continued today," said one trader.
"But the correction is expected to end early next week," he added.
